title: MarketX research log
intro: Living record of every test: what was asked, the pass mark set before it ran, what came out and what it means. Numbers are after costs unless marked gross. Nothing is edited after the fact; corrections get a new entry.
rules: Goal: at least 1% a day on capital. Every result is reported against it, including the gap.
No hindsight: each test year is predicted only from earlier years (walk-forward); saved forecasts are never recomputed.
Real costs: delivery about 0.30% round trip + 0.10% slippage each way; intraday 0.06% + 0.05% each way; stop exits pay another 0.05%. Futures costs come with the F&O work.
Baselines every time: random, simple momentum, Nifty buy-and-hold.
Known bias in tests T1-T8: the stock list was today's Nifty 500 (stocks that later fell out or delisted are missing), which flatters absolute returns. The all-NSE work (R1-R2) removes it.
plan: Agreed 29 Oct 2026: data, then research, then screens. Data: D1 all NSE cash 2015 on (with delistings, split/bonus adjusted, liquidity floor you set, default Rs 5 crore a day); D2 F&O history 2015 on (futures per expiry, options OI, participant positions, near-month series); D3 S&P 500, Nasdaq, Nikkei. Screens after research: all NSE in every page, Live for the 1,000 most liquid, and a separate F&O section.

items.title: Market Lab as built (24 saved nights)
items.question: Do Market Lab's nightly picks make money after costs?
items.pass_mark: Simulate: beat Nifty after costs over the saved nights.
items.headline: Top 10, 1-day hold: Rs 1 lakh -> Rs 84,171 (-15.8%) vs Nifty -2.5%. All 24 setups lost money.
items.notes: The radar predicts 'moves at least 1% either way' (volatility), not direction; the lean was 'unclear' almost every night, so buy-only can't use it.

items.title: Framework diagnostic
items.question: Is the analysis framework the weak link? Which inputs carry direction?
items.pass_mark: Find inputs whose link to next-day relative return keeps its sign in at least 10 of 12 years (|t| >= 3), and compare methods on the same data.
items.headline: Stable signals found (reversal, volatility, gap fade, sector strength, results day, delivery). Equal-weight matching 0.014 vs boosting 0.051: the framework captured about a quarter of what is there.
numbers: After strong up / down results day, 5 days
items.notes: Stable 12/12 years: big 1-5 day movers do worse next day; volatile stocks do worse; opening gaps fade intraday (strongest); strong sector -> stock does better; results day -> stock lags; delivery % up -> better. News tone very weak. Filings on average give no buy signal; first reaction to results continues for 5 days.

items.title: Model v2: daily backtest 2019-2026
items.question: With a learned model, do daily books make money after costs?
items.pass_mark: Positive after costs in every year group, beating random and momentum.
items.headline: On paper: intraday long top 10 / short bottom 10 +0.23% a day, worst drop -9%, no losing year. Later failed the stress test (T4).
numbers: Buy top 10, sell next close, boosting
items.notes: Buy-only next-day: costs (about 0.4% a day) dominate and gains came in 2020-21, negative in 2025-26. Superseded by T4.

items.title: Stress test of the intraday long-short
items.question: Does the T3 intraday edge survive realistic entry and liquidity?
items.pass_mark: Still positive after costs with entry at 09:20, liquid 200 only and 0.10% slippage per side.
items.headline: Gone: all 500 at 09:20 +0.04% a day; liquid 200 at 09:20 -0.05%; everything negative at 0.10% slippage.
items.notes: The 'edge' lived in the noisy opening print of thinly traded stocks. Not tradeable. Parked.

items.title: Swing, buy-only, hold 5 / 10 / 20 sessions
items.question: Is there a swing edge after costs on liquid stocks?
items.pass_mark: Beat Nifty after costs in at least 6 of 8 years with a worst drop no worse than about Nifty's.
items.headline: Simple rules, hold 20, top 10: 25.0% a year vs Nifty 8.3%, beat Nifty 8 of 8 years, worst drop -36% (Nifty -33%).
items.notes: ML not needed for swing: simple rules are the most consistent and explainable.

items.title: Swing robustness
items.question: Does T5 hold for other start days, sizes, costs and a market filter?
items.pass_mark: Every start day beats Nifty overall; at least 5 of 8 years.
items.headline: Hold 20 / 15 stocks: 16.4 / 19.0 / 23.9% a year (lowest / average / highest start day) vs Nifty 10%; 5-7 of 8 years. 2025 weak in every version.
items.notes: Built as Market Lab -> Swing picks (15 stocks, hold 20 sessions): rebuilt 2019-2026 22.3% a year vs Nifty 10.0%, worst drop -28.6%. About 0.08% a day: far below the 1% target.

items.title: Intraday with stop-loss and targets
items.question: Can 3-5 morning setups a day with hard stops reach the 1% target with margin?
items.pass_mark: At least +0.2% a day net at 1x (so about 1% at 5x) with no losing year.
items.headline: Best: 3 trades at 09:30, hold to 15:15: +0.06% a day at 1x; +0.30% at 5x with a -95% worst drop; 2 losing years of 8.
items.notes: The model leans on market-wide inputs (VIX, how the market opened, breadth): it is mostly calling the day's direction. Baselines (momentum, gap fade, random) all lose.

items.title: Day direction
items.question: Can the market's 09:30 -> 15:15 direction be called before or at 09:30?
items.pass_mark: Right on at least 56% of days in every year group.
items.headline: 52-54% right vs 51% always-up. Ceiling: if the direction were known, the intraday picks earn +0.58% a day at 1x, no losing year.
items.notes: The day's direction is the main lever toward 1%. Not yet tried: S&P 500 / Nasdaq / Nikkei (download added), GIFT Nifty, FII/DII flows, F&O positioning: that is R3.
